name: Maelstrom-Vault
description: Maelstrom-Vault is a colossus of banded amber and rust, wrapped in storm lanes wider than most star systems' habitable zones. At its southern latitudes churns the Vault itself—a cyclonic abyss the size of forty worlds, its cloud walls descending farther than any probe has survived to measure. Lightning the breadth of continents stitches between the belts in silence, unseen by anything but the ring of shattered satellites above.

There is no surface to hate here, only layers of fury. Descending through the atmosphere means passing through decks of pressure and wind, each one howling a different note as the hydrogen thickens toward darkness. The magnetic poles sing into every hull that comes close, inducing currents that make instruments lie and tempers fray.

Nobody knows who planted the automated beacon orbiting inside the debris ring, broadcasting a slow prime-number sequence toward the planet's core. Every survey drone sent after the signal has been swallowed by shear winds or simply stopped transmitting at the same depth. The old fuel consortiums call it a malfunction; the crews who have heard it call it an invitation.

The reason anyone endures the Maelstrom is simple: exotic matter condensates form in the Vault's eye, trace flecks worth more than a colony ship, skimmed by hardy harvest rigs on screaming dive trajectories. Helium-3 pays the bills, but the deep flecks buy whole fleets. The storms decide who returns—each season the rigs launch heavier, fly lower, and come back fewer.
